question: Does one private live-winner-or-insert helper reduce duplicated policy without an unacceptable ownership, lock, allocation or interface cost?
inputs: Frozen baseline-dentry.rs and six-test fixture/results from cache-transaction-fixture-01; direct source dependencies only
designs: Single private Cow<str> helper owning children guard; wrapper-specific admission and retention remain outside
checks: Raw live-winner selection including PAR, expired and absent insertion
Owned name moved on insertion, borrowed name materialized only on miss, no extra candidate clone
Guard release before retention and ownership/destruction ordering on each branch
Policy stays in wrappers and no public type/trait or callback interface added
Common invariant centralized versus extra helper, branches, concepts and nonblank lines; no weighted quality score
execution_boundary: Static admission and exact proposal artifact only. No candidate kernel run unless separately admitted and frozen. Existing fixture success is not candidate equivalence.
budget: One concrete proposal, one independent source review; no redesign loop or generic ownership framework
decision: State behavioral gaps separately from maintainability judgment. If unresolved adoption-changing ordering/cost issue remains, retain hypothesis but do not promote to a refactoring recommendation. Missing proof is not proof of a production defect.
stop: Close this proposal after review. If rejected, return to research-stage bottleneck; do not repair with Option state, return guards or wider production interface merely to obtain a positive result.
